                     </ns0:gap> that is with <ns0:hi>common Hands.</ns0:hi> We translate it, <ns0:hi>Polluted,</ns0:hi> so <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.14. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 11.8. Hands not first separated to God by the Religious Rite of washings.</ns0:note>

                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:245" />3 But he answered, and said unto them, Why do you also transgress the commandement of God by your traditions?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.9. tho a little of the Or<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der in which <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> hath it. <ns0:hi>Full well you reject the Commandement of God, that you may keep your own Tradi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour could have answered them, had he pleased more strictly to their Questions, but he must then, either, have incurred Danger, or <ns0:hi>Odium</ns0:hi>; he therefore chuseth to an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer them by another Question, which struck at the Root of the matter. Admit, saith he, my Disciples culpable in not obser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving <ns0:hi>Traditions,</ns0:hi> which indeed you call the <ns0:hi>Traditions</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Elders,</ns0:hi> but are your own, devised by you, or some like you, meerly to uphold your Power and Authority, and to keep People in a needless Subjection to you: I am sure you are far more Guilty, in making <ns0:hi>Traditions</ns0:hi> contrary to the Law of God, or rejecting Gods Law, to keep your <ns0:hi>Tradi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions</ns0:hi>: And indeed this is the common Guilt of those, who are great Zealots for <ns0:hi>Traditions</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Rites,</ns0:hi> not commanded in the word of God. The Jewish <ns0:hi>Rabbi Iose</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>He sin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neth as much, who Eateth with unwashen Hands, as he that lyeth with an Harlot.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> make it a greater sin, for a <ns0:hi>Priest</ns0:hi> to Marry, than to <ns0:hi>keep a Concubine</ns0:hi>; and com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mit <ns0:hi>Fornication</ns0:hi>: They make it a lesser Transgression, than to <ns0:hi>Eat meat on a Friday.</ns0:hi>

               <ns0:p n="5">5 But ye say, Whosoever shall say to <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther or his mother, <ns0:hi>It is</ns0:hi> a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 And honour not his father or mother, <ns0:hi>he shall be free,</ns0:hi> Thus have you made the commande<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment of God, of none effect by your tradition.<ns0:note place="bottom">

Mark</ns0:hi> saith: <ns0:hi>It is Corban [that is, a Gift] Mark</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 12. <ns0:hi>And you suffer him no more to do ought for his Father or Mother,</ns0:hi> which more fully sheweth their Crime, and expoundeth what <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> had said more shortly. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> adds, And <ns0:hi>many such like Things do you.</ns0:hi> This is an instance, by which our Saviour justifi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth his Charge upon them, that they had made void the Law of God by their Traditions. The Law he instanceth in, is the fifth Commandement, <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 20.12. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 5.16. which the Apostle calleth the <ns0:hi>First Commandement with Promise, Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.2. which God had fortified with a <ns0:hi>Iudicial Law,</ns0:hi> wherein he had commanded, <ns0:hi>That he who Cursed his Father and Mother should be put to Death, Exod.</ns0:hi> 21.17. <ns0:hi>Levit.</ns0:hi> 20.9. he had also further threatned the Violaters of this Law, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 20.20. By the way our Saviour here al<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o lets us know, that the fifth Commandement obligeth Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren to relieve their Parents in their necessity, and this is the Sense of the term, <ns0:hi>Honour,</ns0:hi> in other Texts of Scripture. A Law of God, which hath approved it self to the Wisdom almost of all Nations. <ns0:hi>Liberi Parentes alant aut vinciantur.</ns0:hi> Let Children relieve their Parents, or be put into Prison, was an old <ns0:hi>Roman Law.</ns0:hi> Nor did the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> deny this in terms, but they had made an <ns0:hi>Exception</ns0:hi> from it, which in Effect made it of no use, at least such as wicked Children ea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ily might, and commonly did elude it by: They had taught the People to say to their Parents, <ns0:hi>Corban: It is a Gift, by whatsoever thou mayst be profited by me:</ns0:hi> And in that Case, tho they did not give their poor Parents any thing wherewith they might relieve their Necessities, yet they should be Guiltless as to the fifth <ns0:hi>Commandement.</ns0:hi> There is a strange Variety of Interpreters as to this Text. Some making the Sense this, <ns0:hi>That which I should relieve you with, I have dedicated unto God, and therefore I cannot relieve you:</ns0:hi> Others thus, <ns0:hi>I have dedicated my Estate to God, and that will be as much Good, and benefit to you, as if I had given it unto you.</ns0:hi> Others think that <ns0:hi>Corban</ns0:hi> was the form of an <ns0:hi>Oath,</ns0:hi> from whence they form other Senses. But the most Free, and unconstrained Sense seemeth to be this. The <ns0:hi>Pha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />risees</ns0:hi> were a very Courteous Generation, and had a share in the <ns0:hi>Gifts,</ns0:hi> that were brought unto God, for the use of the Temple or otherwise, thence they were very <ns0:hi>Zealous,</ns0:hi> and diligent in perswading People to make such Oblations, when any pretended the need that their Parents stood in of their help, they told them, That i<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> they told their Parents, <ns0:hi>it was a Gift</ns0:hi> that they had vowed, such a Portion of their Estate to a sacred use, that would before God excuse them for not relieving their Parents; so as the Precept of <ns0:hi>Honour<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing their Parents,</ns0:hi> and relieving them in their nece<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sities, obliged them not, if they had first given to God the things by which their Parents might, or ought to have been reliev<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">

                     </ns0:gap>lighting of all external Rites and Actions, not at<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tended with a sutable inward Homage, and Devotion of Heart.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 But he answered, and said, Every plant which my heavenly <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 15.2.</ns0:note> Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Let them alone <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 23.14.16. Luk. 6.39.</ns0:note> they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Every Plant,</ns0:hi> may be understood of <ns0:hi>Doctrines, Practi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ces,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Persons.</ns0:hi> These <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> are a wretch<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed Generation, that a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e got into the Sheep-fold, not <ns0:hi>at the Door,</ns0:hi> my Father never sent them, they are crept in at the Windows, they are Plants got into my Garden, which my Father never <ns0:hi>Planted</ns0:hi> there, and they must be Rooted up <ns0:hi>Let them alone,</ns0:hi> they are incorrigible, and blinded by their own Interest against any Conviction, or Instruction, as <ns0:hi>Hos.</ns0:hi> 4.17. <ns0:hi>Ephraim is joyn'd to Idols, let him alone.</ns0:hi> So these Men are joyned to their Superstitious Traditions: I will not concern my self with them: They are pretended <ns0:hi>Leaders of the Blind, Rom.</ns0:hi> 2.19. but themselves are Blind. I pity the poor People, for whilst the Blind lead the Blind, they both fall into a Ditch. An ignorant and unfaithful Ministry is the greatest Plague God can send amongst a People.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mark 7.17.</ns0:note> Then answered Peter, and said unto him, Declare unto us this parable.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And Jesus said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.9.</ns0:note> Are ye also yet without understanding?<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>His Disciples asked him concerning the Pa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rable, Peter</ns0:hi> probably began, the rest follow<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d. Or, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> speaks in the Name of the rest, for our Saviour in his An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swer, doth not say, <ns0:hi>Art thou,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>are ye.</ns0:hi> They did well, in that they desired to be instructed what the mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing was of the <ns0:hi>Parable,</ns0:hi> that is, the dark saying, which he used (for the <ns0:hi>Hebrews</ns0:hi> called all dark Sayings, Parables) possibly they might also stumble at what our Saviour said, as tending to the Destruction of the <ns0:hi>Ceremonial Law,</ns0:hi> a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bout the difference of Meats. But that they were no bet<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter instructed, than not to understand a thing so plain and obvious, this was their Fault, and argued their small im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />provement of our Saviours Company. God expects a profi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciency in knowledge from us, proportionate unto the means he giveth us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entreth in at the mouth, goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jam. 3.6.</ns0:note> those things, which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart, and they defile a man.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 6.5. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 8.21. Prov. 6.14. Jer. 17.9.</ns0:note> For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>wit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness, blasphemies.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands, defileth not a man.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath this<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> with very small difference in Words, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23. only he specifieth some more sins, than <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> enumerateth. The Sum of what our Saviour <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>aith is this. That all sin proceedeth from Lust, some de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sires in the Heart of man after things forbidden in the Law of God. All the t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>cklings of our Hearts, with such Thoughts, all the Willings, and De<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>res of such things, tho they never issue in Over-Acts, yet de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ile, and pollute a Man, and from these inward Motions of the Heart, proceed those Overt-Acts (mentioned by <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi>) of <ns0:hi>Murders, Adul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />teries, Fornication, Theft, False-witness, Blasphemy, De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceit, L<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>scivousness, an Evil Eye, Pride, Foolishness,</ns0:hi> now these things take them in their Nest, which is the Heart, they de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />file, and pollute that. Take them in their passage through our Lips, into the World<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> they pollute that, take them in their <ns0:hi>Overt-Act,</ns0:hi> they pollute the Man. But to eat with <ns0:hi>unwashen Hands,</ns0:hi> a thing no where forbidden by God, only by the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> who had no such Authority given them from God, to command any such things, this doth not pul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lute a Man. It is po<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sible, that Men may sin in not obey<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing the Commandements of Men, but it must be than in things, in which God hath Authorized them to command, and to determine our Practice in, for the pollution lyes in a Disobedience, to the Commandement of God, not of Men.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 Then Jesus went thence, and departed into the coasts of Tyre and Sidon.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.24. addeth, <ns0:hi>and entred into an House, and would have no Man know of it, but he could not be hid:</ns0:hi> Some here make a Question, whether our Saviour did go in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to <ns0:hi>Phoenicia</ns0:hi> (of which <ns0:hi>Tyre</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sidon</ns0:hi> were the principal Cities) or only into the Coasts of <ns0:hi>Palestina</ns0:hi> next to it; those that think he did not go into <ns0:hi>Phoenicia,</ns0:hi> are guided by his Prohibition of his Disciples, to <ns0:hi>go into the way of the Gentiles, Mat.</ns0:hi> 10.5. and the Consideration, that the time was not yet come, for his manifestation to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> I rather incline to think, that he went into <ns0:hi>Tyre</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sidon</ns0:hi>; and that this was a kind of a <ns0:hi>Praeludium</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>calling of the Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and a Prediction of what should be done more fully after<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards: It is manifest he did not go with a design to make himself publick there, for <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, he <ns0:hi>would have no Man know of it.</ns0:hi> But for privacy withdrew himself thi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, and shewed some of his miraculous Operations there, and <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 22. Saith the Woman that came to him was a <ns0:hi>C<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                        <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naanite, Mark</ns0:hi> saith, she was a <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Syrophenician</ns0:hi> by Nation. Nor is here any Contradiction, for ever since the <ns0:hi>Grecian Monarchy,</ns0:hi> prevailed over so great a part of the World. The Name of <ns0:hi>Greeks</ns0:hi> had obtained, so as they called all <ns0:hi>Greeks</ns0:hi> who were not <ns0:hi>Iews, Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.14.16. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.12. a <ns0:hi>Syro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phenician</ns0:hi> saith <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Nation</ns0:hi>: That is, one that was a Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive of that part of <ns0:hi>Phoenicia,</ns0:hi> which is joyned to <ns0:hi>Tyre</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sidon. Matthew</ns0:hi> calls her a <ns0:hi>Canaanite,</ns0:hi> or a Woman of <ns0:hi>Ca<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />naan,</ns0:hi> by which tho some would understand one of <ns0:hi>Cana,</ns0:hi> yet as the <ns0:hi>Orthography</ns0:hi> will not agree, so <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> calling her a <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> and a <ns0:hi>Syrophenician,</ns0:hi> inclines us rather to judge her of the stock of the Old <ns0:hi>Canaanites.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mar. 7.25.26.</ns0:note> behold a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cryed unto him, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, Have mercy on me O Lord, thou son of Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vid; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But he answered her not a word, And his disciples came, and besought him, saying, Send her away; for she cryeth after us.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, A <ns0:hi>certain Woman whose young Daughter had an unclean Spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his Feet<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> The Woman was a Greek a Syrophenician by Nation, and she besought him, that he would cast forth the Devil out of her Daughter. But Iesus said unto her, let the Children first be filled, for it is not meet to take the Childrens Bread, and to cast it to Dogs. Mark</ns0:hi> 7.25, 26, 27. Tho the Woman appears to have been a <ns0:hi>Pagan,</ns0:hi> yet living so near <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> she had doubtless heard of Christ, both what he had done in casting out Devils, and also that he was lookt upon as the <ns0:hi>Son of David,</ns0:hi> and usually called by that Name, by those who went to him for any Cures; she therefore gives him that Title: Others, think her to have been more specially in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lightned, and to have called him the Son of <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> not as an usual Compellation given him, but as believing him to have been the true <ns0:hi>Messias</ns0:hi> promised to the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> nor <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>s that im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />possible, for tho the Gospel at this time had not shined out upon any Considerable number of the Heathen, yet God in all times had his number amongst them, and this Woman living so near to the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and so near to <ns0:hi>Galilee,</ns0:hi> where our Saviour hitherto had most Conversed, and Preached, it is not improbable, that she might have received the <ns0:hi>Grace,</ns0:hi> as well as the sound of the Gospel, so God might have kindled in <ns0:hi>her</ns0:hi> Heart, a true Faith in the <ns0:hi>Messias.</ns0:hi> Our Saviours Commendation of her Faith in the following Discourse, ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />keth this very probable. <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, that he <ns0:hi>answered her not a Word, Mark</ns0:hi> saith, that he said to her, <ns0:hi>Let the Children first be filled,</ns0:hi> &c. To the observing Reader, this will appear no Contradiction. For by <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> it should appear, that she first came to our Saviour into the House, into which he went, that he might be private, and there fell at his Feet Here Christ <ns0:hi>answered her not a Word</ns0:hi>; took no notice of her at all, But it appeareth by <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> that Christ soon left the House, and she followed after him upon the way. The Disciples said, <ns0:hi>send her away, for she cryeth after us.</ns0:hi> Then it was that our Saviour said to her, <ns0:hi>Let the Children be first filled.</ns0:hi> His Disciples <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rst interposing, saying, <ns0:hi>send her away, for she cryeth after us.</ns0:hi> How any of the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> think that this Text Patronizeth their <ns0:hi>Invocation</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Saints</ns0:hi> departed, I cannot tell, for these Disciples were alive, and we do not read, that she spake to any of them, to intercetrans for her<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> It is certain they did move Christ on her behalf.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:246" />24 But he answered, and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 10.5, 6.</ns0:note> I am not sent, but to the lost sheep of Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord by these Words doth not deny, but that he was sent as a <ns0:hi>Redeemer</ns0:hi> to more, but <ns0:hi>not as a Minister</ns0:hi> or as an <ns0:hi>A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postle,</ns0:hi> as he is called, <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 3.1. The Apostle <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 15.8. saith, <ns0:hi>That Iesus Christ was a Minister of the Circumcision, for the Truth of God, to confirm the promises made to the Fathers.</ns0:hi> Our Lords Ministry was confined to the Jews, so was the Apostles, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 10.5. Till some time after our S<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viours Ascension, the <ns0:hi>Gospel</ns0:hi> was not Preached generally to the Gentiles, tho some particular Persons might, and did both in Christs time, and in the time of the <ns0:hi>Ap<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>stles,</ns0:hi> before they did go to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> hear, receive, and imbrace the Gospel, as we shall hear this Woman did.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Then came she, and worshipped him, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, Lord, help me.<ns0:note place="bottom">She here acknowledgeth his <ns0:hi>Divine Power,</ns0:hi> and imploreth his <ns0:hi>Help.</ns0:hi> Thus shewing that she believed him to be the Son of God, and a rewarder of those that sought him, and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tinues her request after two Repulses.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 But he answered, and said, It is not meet to take the childrens bread, and to cast it to dogs.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 7.27. <ns0:hi>Iesus said unto her, Let the Children first be filled, for it is not meet,</ns0:hi> &c. By the <ns0:hi>Chil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dren,</ns0:hi> here he means the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>Dogs,</ns0:hi> he meaneth the <ns0:hi>Heathen.</ns0:hi> The Jews are called the Children of the Kingdom, <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> is called <ns0:hi>Gods Son, his first Born, Exod.</ns0:hi> 4.22. the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 9.4. saith, to them <ns0:hi>belong'd the Adoption.</ns0:hi> By Bread here our Saviour means, the <ns0:hi>Publication of the Gospel,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Miracles</ns0:hi> by which the truth of the Doctrine of it was confirmed, by <ns0:hi>Dogs,</ns0:hi> he means the Heathen, whom the Jews did count as Dogs, no Members of the Houshold of God, it was a Term of Contempt, 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 3.8. and 16.9. 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 8.13. When our Saviour saith <ns0:hi>it is not Meet,</ns0:hi> he means it is not just, nor equal, <ns0:hi>Obj.</ns0:hi> How came it then, that the Gospel was ever carried to the Gentiles? <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> Expounds our Savi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ours meaning, or rather gives us an account of our Saviours Words more perfectly. <ns0:hi>Let the Children be first filled. It is not Meet,</ns0:hi> &c. The Jews are Gods Children, a People whom he chose out of all the Nations of the Earth, to whom he gave ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny Priviledges. It is his Will the Gospel should be first Preached to them, and then to the Gentiles. Gentiles are as Dogs, of whom God hath not taken such a care, but they shall have their time. Only it is not Consonant to my Fathers Will, that the Gospel, and the Miracles by which it is confirmed, should be Exhibited unto you Gentiles, till it hath been fully Preached to the Jews, and they be first filled with the Sound, and with the Confirmations of it.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 And she said, Truth Lord, yet the dogs eat of the crumbs, which fall from their masters ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> reports it to the same Sense, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 7.28. She goeth on after a third Repulse. The last of which was not without a reproach, for our Lord had implicitely call'd her a <ns0:hi>Dog.</ns0:hi> These words are as much, as if she had said, Lord, I confess the Jews are <ns0:hi>Children.</ns0:hi> I am a <ns0:hi>Dog,</ns0:hi> a poor Heathen, no proper Member of the Houshold of God, and it is Truth, that it seemeth unreasonable, that I being a Dog, should be served before all the Children are filled. Lord, I do not beg such a full Manifestation of thy power, and goodness for the Gentiles, I beg but a Crumb of Mercy for my self, and poor Child, and <ns0:hi>Lord,</ns0:hi> tho we do not use to give our Loaves prepared for our Children, to the Dogs that feed under our Table, <ns0:hi>Crumbs</ns0:hi> of our Childrens Bread, as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> express<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth it, yet we Suffer our Dogs to gather them up. Lord, I know thou hast a plenty of Grace, and Blessing, the Children may be filled, and yet I may have some Crumbs. Three things are Remarkable in her Answer, besides her Faith so emi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nently expressed. 1. Her <ns0:hi>Humility,</ns0:hi> she owneth herself a <ns0:hi>Dog.</ns0:hi> 2. Her <ns0:hi>Modesty,</ns0:hi> she beggeth no more than a <ns0:hi>Crumb.</ns0:hi> 3. Her <ns0:hi>Fervency,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Importunity</ns0:hi> after three Repulses. By this we Learn our Duty in Prayer, to go to God Humbly, to implore him modestly, and to be instant in Prayer, going on in our Duty, tho we have not presently such an Answer as we desire. These things conjoyned with Faith, make an acceptable Prayer,</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 Then Jesus said unto her, O woman! great <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> thy faith; be it unto thee, even as thou wilt. And her daughter was made whole from that very hour.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 7.29. <ns0:hi>And he said unto her, for this saying, Go thy way, the Devil is gone out of thy Daughter. And when she was come to her House, she found the Devil gone out, and her Daughter laid up<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n the Bed.</ns0:hi> O Woman! for this saying, shewing the greatness of thy Faith. Be it unto thee, as thou wilt. Go thy way, the Devil is gone out of thy Daughter. And her Daughter was made whole that very Hour, as she understood, when she came home to her House, for she found the Devil was gone out of her Daugh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter, and her Daughter was laid upon the Bed. Thus the Words of both the Evangelists Compounded, make but one entire and perfect Sense. The greatness of her Faith appeared in two things. 1. In that she had so little means, so small a Revela<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, being a Pagan, she ordinarily had not heard the Gospel, nor seen so many of Christs mighty Works, Confirming the Truth of the Doctrine of it. Hence it is o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>served, that Christ admired the Faith of none but <ns0:hi>Pagans. Matth.</ns0:hi> 8.10.2. In that she would not give over, tho he gave her three Repul<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses. So as she said like <ns0:hi>Iacob. I will not let thee go, until thou Bless me.</ns0:hi> And as he like a <ns0:hi>Prince,</ns0:hi> so she like a <ns0:hi>Princess</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> prevailed with God, and obtained the thing which she desired, But will some say. <ns0:hi>Where was her Faith?</ns0:hi> What promise? what Word of God had she to assent to? God doth not speak to us outwardly, but inwardly, as undoubtedly he had to this Woman, giving her some inward assurance, that he was the <ns0:hi>Son of God,</ns0:hi> and both able, and willing to grant her the thing she asked. Now a f<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rm and fixed assent to any Divine Reve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation is Faith: whether the Revelation be <ns0:hi>Internal</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Exter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal.</ns0:hi> We from hence learn, the mighty Power of <ns0:hi>True Faith</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Fervent Prayer.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And Jesus departed from thence, and came nigh unto the sea of Galilee, and went up into a mountain, and sate down there.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And great multitudes came unto him, ha<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving with them those that were <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 35.5, 6.                <ns0:p n="31">31 Insomuch that the multitude wondred, when they saw the dumb to speak, the maimed to be whole, the lame to walk, and the blind to see, And they glorified the God of Israel.<ns0:note place="bottom">

               <ns0:p n="32">32 Then Jesus called his disciples unto him, and said, I have compassion on the multitude, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat, and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="39">39 And he sent away the multitude, and took ship, and came into the coasts of Magdala.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> gives us an account of this Mircale, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> There is very little difference in their Relations, only <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, our Saviour went into the Coasts of <ns0:hi>Dalma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nutha, Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, in the Coasts of <ns0:hi>Magdala,</ns0:hi> most think that it was the same place which had two Names, some think one was the Name of the Country, the other, of the City or Town.                      </ns0:gap>e question how they could fast three Days, but the Text doth not say so, only that at that time they had nothing to eat, having spent wh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t they brought with them probably in their Baskets, which Answers another question also, how they could get Baskets in the Wilderness. The Miracle was of the same Nature, with that which we met with, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14. Only there were 5000 Men fed with five Loaves, and two Fishes, here 4000 were fed with seven Loaves, and a few Fishes, there they took up twelve, here but seven Baskets full. Our Lord worketh sometimes without means, sometimes by means, and those differently proportioneth to his end, as it pleaseth him. The Miraculous Operations of our Saviour, are amongst his <ns0:hi>Miranda</ns0:hi> et <ns0:hi>Ado<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />randa,</ns0:hi> not his <ns0:hi>Imitanda.</ns0:hi> These Actions of his, which we are in reading to admire, and adore, but are not concerned to imitate, yet something we may observe from them, both for our <ns0:hi>Instruction</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Imitation.</ns0:hi> For our Instruction, we may from this History observe the Extent of Christs Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />passion to his Disciples, which tho it is most Eminently seen in what he doth for their Souls, yet reacheth also to their Bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dies, and more External wants. It also teacheth us to trust God in the doing of our Duty. Those that are in a Wilderness hearing Christ, shall not faint by the way, before they get home. His course of giving Thanks before he brake, and made use of the Bread (which we observed before in the other Miracle) commendeth to us, the religious Custom of begging a Blessing before our Meat, and giving Thanks to God for good things, of that Nature, when we have received them.</ns0:note>
